description:
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hello, I made this team with the help of Claude!
We are hoping to make learning about space easy and fun for children!
In order to accomplish this, I have created an interactive website with the help of several sub agents and Fable 5.2.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
summary: Still Up There is an interactive 3D website that tells school-age children the story of the hardware NASA has left on the Moon and Mars. Guided by Hy, a hydrogen-atom detective, the child completes six quests instead of reading pages: walking the Moon to find four machines, firing a laser at an Apollo mirror to measure the Moon’s distance, driving Perseverance and Curiosity and flying Ingenuity, naming spacecrafts, interviewing machines, and being able to understand which facts are real or fake. Each quest ends with recall questions, so the child leaves remembering what the hardware did and the science it made possible. It matters because these machines are still up there, abandoned, but not forgotten.
details:
What it does. The site opens with Hy introducing a case: machines NASA left behind. Six quests follow in order, and each stop opens only when the one before is done.🔥

1. 🌑 Moon walk: find the Apollo 15 laser mirror, the Apollo 17 Moon car, Surveyor 3 and the LCROSS crash site.

2. 🔦Laser: aim at the Moon, build a three-mirror corner reflector, and match the 2.5-second echo to measure 384,400 km.

3. 🪨⛏️ Mars: drill a rock core as Perseverance, analyse powder in Curiosity’s onboard lab and radio the result home, then fly Ingenuity and relay photos through an orbiter.

4. 👤 Whose shadow: identify seven spacecraft from their silhouettes.

5. 🗣️💬Spend time with Hy: a Moon tour, a mystery machine, or an interview with a machine.

6. ❌✅ Distinguish between a lies and truths : eight claims to judge.

Finishing all six plays a 3D ending in which Hy crosses the solar system and gives the child a medal. 🏆
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

👍- Benefits and impact. Children learn by doing, with very little text, and every quest checks recall. Hy steps in automatically when a child is stuck for ten seconds. The intended impact is that a child can explain, afterwards, what a retroreflector does, why Mars samples are still on Mars, and why a helicopter needs fast blades in thin air.

🔨 - Tools. HTML, CSS and JavaScript with three.js (WebGL) for all 3D scenes; NASA 3D Resources models converted with Blender and glTF tools; hosted as a static site on Render; ElevenLabs for Hy’s voice; Claude for coding assistance; used Github to create a repository; information from NASA data/websites.

💡 - Creativity. The content is a story with one character, not a catalogue. Each fact learned by doing something yourself : building the mirrors to reflect back the laser, powering Curiosity and Perseverence rovers, flying Ingenuity.

🎯 - What we considered. Accuracy first: where reality differs from a neat story we show reality, for example the Mars sample return is labelled as a plan that has not flown. We also considered young readers (short sentences, spoken lines), phones and laptops, reduced-motion settings, and a version that works without 3D graphics. All facts link to their NASA sources on the site.
